correctness.rationale: Under positive utilities u=n-r, Gale-Shapley men-optimality gives every changed man a strict loss: u_T/u_M<= (n-1)/n; exactly the same k women change, each with ratio at most n. Hence P(T)/P(M)<=(n-1)^k and the root welfare ratio <=sqrt(n-1). The explicit changed-k cyclic construction realizes equality for every 2<=k<=n. For n>=3 equality in the global n-power bound forces k=n and each man first/second and woman last/first partners, proving exactly n!D_n((n-2)!)^(2n) labeled extremizers and unique optimal T. For n=2 any stable alternative has product ratio 1. Independent brute enumeration computed n=2:16 and n=3:46656 complete preference profiles, n=3 12 extremizers and 5424 strict improvements; no finite check is used as all-n proof.
residual_risks: Finite experiments corroborate only their tested cases; unlimited parameter conclusions use the reconstructed proof.
